rationale: Neither candidate hits the ground truth's core concerns (missing profiling/VRAM evidence, the streaming native-speed-rejection bug, WebSocket/HTTP asymmetry, duration_factor bound duplication across files, or the benchmark-script-vs-registry question) — both reviewed different, largely orthogonal territory, so recall is low for both. X produces fewer but higher-stakes, highly actionable findings (uninitialized mel_head.bias, silent zero-audio path, IndexTTS-2.0 regression table) with concrete patches, but they are unverifiable against the visible diff and X entirely skips the benchmarks/docs portion actually shown. Y produces more numerous, evidence-quoted findings (test-marker deselection, Spanish TN fallback, version/Test-Plan mismatch) that are better grounded methodologically and closer in topic to the adapter/duration_factor area GT cares about, but skews toward process/doc nits rather than deep bugs and is less concretely actionable. The trade-offs roughly cancel out.
